projects.name: Neon Dash 2
projects.description: A mobile endless runner prototype exploring responsive controls, procedural track generation, and performance-aware object pooling.
projects.overview: A compact mobile prototype built to investigate how input feel, pacing, and runtime efficiency work together in an endless runner. All project details shown are sample portfolio content.

sections.title: The goal
sections.body: Create a readable, responsive runner loop suitable for short mobile sessions while keeping the project structured for rapid iteration.

sections.title: Development process
sections.body: I separated tuning data from runtime logic, then iterated on movement feel with a small test course before adding procedural segments and obstacles.

sections.title: Technical implementation
sections.body: Track segments are requested through a pool and positioned from authored connection points. Difficulty data changes spawn weights without altering generation code.

sections.title: Problem → solution
sections.body: Rapid spawning caused frame-time spikes in the first pass. The sample solution pre-warms reusable objects and spreads non-critical setup work across frames.

projects.name: Relay Protocol
projects.description: A networked interaction and inventory framework focused on authority, replication, and clear designer-facing extension points.
projects.overview: A sample multiplayer systems case study demonstrating how a portfolio can communicate architecture, trade-offs, and cross-discipline collaboration.

sections.title: The goal
sections.body: Design a reusable interaction layer and authoritative inventory that remains understandable to designers working in Blueprints.

sections.title: Development process
sections.body: I mapped ownership and RPC boundaries first, prototyped a single pickup flow, then expanded the API only after validating server and client behavior.

sections.title: Technical implementation
sections.body: The server owns inventory mutation. Clients request interactions, receive replicated state, and update presentation through change events rather than polling.

sections.title: Problem → solution
sections.body: Late-joining clients initially missed transient item presentation. The proposed fix derives presentation from replicated state and uses idempotent refresh logic.

projects.name: Iron Pulse
projects.description: A third-person combat sandbox built to study animation-driven attacks, hit detection, ability state, and combat readability.
projects.overview: A sample combat prototype case study centered on communicating implementation decisions rather than presenting a finished game.

sections.title: The goal
sections.body: Build a small but extensible combat loop with deliberate timing, readable reactions, and tools for diagnosing hit behavior.

sections.title: Development process
sections.body: I began with instrumented attacks and placeholder animation, established state transitions, then tuned timing and feedback after the rules were reliable.

sections.title: Technical implementation
sections.body: Animation notifies open and close attack windows. A per-swing hit set prevents repeated damage while trace debug output exposes missed collisions.

sections.title: Problem → solution
sections.body: Low frame rates could leave gaps between trace samples. The sample approach sweeps between previous and current socket transforms.

projects.name: Echoes Below
projects.description: A data-driven C++ terminal adventure with command parsing, branching encounters, and save-state serialization.
projects.overview: A sample command-line project showing core C++ design, data structures, parsing, and separation of content from game logic.

sections.title: The goal
sections.body: Explore clean C++ architecture without an engine while making narrative content quick to author and validate.

sections.title: Development process
sections.body: I built a tiny vertical slice around look, take, and use commands before generalizing verbs and moving encounter text into data.

sections.title: Technical implementation
sections.body: Tokenized commands resolve through registered actions. Game state is serialized separately from content definitions to keep saves compact.

sections.title: Problem → solution
sections.body: Ambiguous object names created confusing failures. The parser now returns candidate matches and requests clarification.

lessons: Small tools deserve clear error states

projects.name: Signal Garden
projects.description: A compact Pygame puzzle experiment with grid simulation, deterministic updates, and a level-authoring workflow.
projects.overview: A sample small-scope project demonstrating simulation logic, deterministic testing, and iteration tools.

sections.title: The goal
sections.body: Create an approachable puzzle loop where simple rules combine into surprising outcomes.

sections.title: Development process
sections.body: Simulation rules were developed as pure state updates before rendering, making edge cases easier to reproduce and test.

sections.title: Technical implementation
sections.body: Each tick reads from the previous grid and writes to a new state, avoiding order-dependent results.

sections.title: Problem → solution
sections.body: In-place updates produced inconsistent chain reactions. Double-buffering made each simulation step deterministic.

projects.name: Frontline Vector
projects.description: An Unreal RTS prototype exploring selection, command queues, formation movement, and scalable unit decision-making.
projects.overview: A sample RTS case study designed to show systems thinking across input, AI, navigation, and player feedback.

sections.title: The goal
sections.body: Make commanding groups of units feel predictable while keeping unit logic modular enough for new command types.

sections.title: Development process
sections.body: I validated selection and feedback first, added a command abstraction, then profiled group movement under increasing unit counts.

sections.title: Technical implementation
sections.body: Commands carry target context and lifecycle state. Formation slots are assigned before individual path requests to reduce crowding at a single point.

sections.title: Problem → solution
sections.body: Units oscillated while reaching dense formations. Arrival tolerance and stable slot ownership reduced constant replanning.

lessons: Player feedback is part of the control system
